title: Under COMMA_SEPARATED, a comma inside an ordinary scalar string invents an array out of nothing
rationale: The Javadoc warns about delimiter collisions, but only for values inside arrays. The real behaviour is worse: no array need be involved at all. A plain scalar string "Smith, John" triggers looksLikeSerializedArray purely because it contains a comma, the parent becomes an array, and the sibling scalar is duplicated by last-value padding.
catchesBugClass: Reconstructor-side heuristics firing on data the flattener never encoded. Also catches the documentation gap: readers will take the existing warning to mean array elements only.
cannotCatch: Does not test PIPE_SEPARATED, which takes the identical code path with a different character. It also cannot catch the mirror hazard of a genuine COMMA_SEPARATED array whose elements themselves contain commas.

predicted.detail: Flattening does not touch either value; the damage is entirely on the reconstruct side, where the comma splits the name into two array elements and the sibling is padded by repetition.
